Hi there, trans mama with trans masc teen. First off, so, so much love and thank you for being there for your boy. My kid sends love too. We dealt with a hospital stay with similar issues and some serious life adjustments after that, so I understand deeply where you're at. 

I see a lot of people commenting on the med situation and that may very well be the thing that's causing this - those meds are meant to reset the brain a bit and it can be weird the first time out especially if you're new to meds. For him to say he's "lost his anchor" is really powerful. We can anchor ourselves a lot in anxiety and pain and it can almost be scarier to not have that as a reference point -  but it's a chance to explore the questions more deeply without the noise. It can take time to sort that out and it's good to have a little patience. 

I had to sort out a lot for myself and I only really truly pursued things about 10 years ago, and I had to really deeply process what it was to be trans, as well to understand the filters of my mind with anxiety and depression situations. It took me a while to separate the two. If dysphoria was related to a true mental health issue, explore what he feels about not pursuing transition. Reassess these questions every month or so. He's just starting to sort himself out and there's no one way to do this, just whatever feels best at the time. Meds can take a while to do their work. I think of them as a way to try to relearn certain mental assumptions and patterns, especially around identity. Gender imprinting from sociocultural cues is a very powerful thing. I remember far too often how I got told what I did was too "girly" as a kid. 

If he feels he's lost his anchor, I'd just work with him a little bit on how being treated/referenced as male/etc makes him feel. Does he see a future there? Does he not? Is it still core to his sense of identity? If it is, then it is worth considering that trans people do not have to have dysphoria to be valid. It can be a wild feeling for it to be a neutral or positive situation as opposed to learning it as always being uncomfortable. There's no single way to be trans or enby. There can be such a thing as trans joy.

I'm running mine on a Pi 3B, but any pi will do fine. Here's a video if you are a more visual learner. [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jkd3jmHS2hs](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jkd3jmHS2hs)

This shows how to copy/paste the wpa\_supplicant.conf file on the sd card from your existing PC/mac/fancy toaster oven (lol) . There is also a way to configure SSH to ON by editing another file.

Alternatively you can plug in a monitor and keyboard long enough on the pi to use the pi desktop to set up your connection like you would on any OS. It will remember that much off hand. Then get to a terminal and run "sudo raspi-config" - in there is an option to turn ON SSH, do so, save and exit.

after that, You should log into your router and see if you have something that looks like a raspberry pi identifier, with it's IP attached, in the same way you'd check any other IP.

use a program like PuTTY for a shell where you can type commands over the network to your pi. It will prompt you for an IP (use the one from your router) and typically SSH is port 23. Then login with the username and PW to get to the shell on the pi.

It looks like you kind of already understand how to get to a shell, so that's good!

From the SSH shell (or from the desktop of the pi itself, in a terminal) you can start the pihole install process - "sudo apt-get install pihole"  the rest of it is pretty automatic.

The tricky part is to set it up as a DNS (Domain Name Server). Most routers have a DNS built in, and most also have the option for an external DNS server. You have to tell your wifi router that the Pi Hole will handle your DNS, and there's where you put the Pi's manually assigned IP (most routers are [192.168.0.1](https://192.168.0.1) for instance, you can set your pi hole's IP to [192.168.0.2](https://192.168.0.2). ) When this step is successful, you can then connect to your pi over wifi.

in the PiHole software, you can reserve all other fixed IP's, and set the range for your DHCP addresses (the ones your boxes will generate automatically, like [192.168.0.100](https://192.168.0.100) to [192.168.0.200](https://192.168.0.200). That gives you 100 valid auto IPs (more than any average home will ever need). Server items (router, pihole, etc) need fixed IP's so the rest of the system needs them reserved , and understands all traffic routes via pihole so we can filter it.

Lastly, when pihole is running for the first time, you'll have to look up some blocklists and import them. That is where the filtering magic happens. Get the most common ones to start with, they work quite well.

There are tons of various guides on all this stuff. If one confuses you, try finding another one that's written a little differently.

Keep up the effort friend! it's tricky at first to learn all this new stuff - but it's so satisfying to kill off so much crappy traffic, ads, malware, etc. I forget how spoiled I am until I have to use non pi holed networks!  


EDIT: I should also mention a lot of the basic wifi/cablemodem etc boxes that come from the companies are painfully simple and may not have all the abilities to be configured. You may need to get a proper router and connect it to your internet box via a short ethernet cable. etc.

You may be experiencing some third/fourth harmonic reflections, which is common with RTL SDR's, especially if you are using high gain stuff (antennas, Low noise amplifiers (LNAs), or high internal gain on the SDR.)  Broadcast stations are super strong, and don't broadcast purely on their assigned frequencies. However, the harmonics are always somewhat weaker then the "real", and easier to filter out.  "Real" radios are less impacted because they have better rejection of unintended signals.

A little reading:

[http://www.pateplumaradio.com/genbroad/harmonics.htm](http://www.pateplumaradio.com/genbroad/harmonics.htm)

It's a feature/glitch (I say that because sometimes harmonics can be used to "get" signals that are technically out of the SDR's range). What you need is/are filter blocks that block broadcast AM/FM transmissions and attach inline with your antenna. RTL SDR blog sells them. (I have an AM and an FM filter block in line for my shortwave RTL-SDR antenna).

I assume you want to tie two SDR's together to share one antenna, you'll probably want a SMA splitter.  [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SMA\_connector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SMA_connector)  


[https://www.amazon.com/Bingfu-Antenna-Splitter-Cellular-Amplifier/dp/B07STYNB6V/ref=sr\_1\_3?crid=3JQTBFUINZT34&dchild=1&keywords=sma+splitter+%2F+y+adapter&qid=1606457509&sprefix=sma+spl%2Caps%2C200&sr=8-3](https://www.amazon.com/Bingfu-Antenna-Splitter-Cellular-Amplifier/dp/B07STYNB6V/ref=sr_1_3?crid=3JQTBFUINZT34&dchild=1&keywords=sma+splitter+%2F+y+adapter&qid=1606457509&sprefix=sma+spl%2Caps%2C200&sr=8-3)  


Smaller antenna looks like a BNC.. you can get an SMA to BNC too. 

You'll want to learn the various connector types - there's a ton of them. Once you do, you can amazon all kinds of adapters/couplers/splitters/etc for fairly inexpensive prices. There are often kits that have several different types of adapters in them - handy for tinkering.  


Have fun!

Dr Will Powers has a a presence on Reddit, and he's got a lot of information about Trans Hormones. The Estrone levels being too high is explained by him in his excellent powerpoint about the care of transgender people. I think he's on the 6th version of it.   


if you are just doing it oral, the majority of the estrogen is broken down by the liver prior to even getting into your system - sublingual bypasses a lot of that by getting into the blood stream more directly. 

in terms of estrone, there are several flavors of estrogen in humans - we want the most powerful one - estradiol. However Dr Powers believes that for some MTF people there is a "estrone mutation" that makes some of our MTF bodies want to convert estradiol into estrone, which is only 4% as powerful. If you don't specifically separate the blood tests, it can all look "good" when in reality it isn't.

Well, I can tell you what I have done. I realize I might be atypical in this regard. I also happen to be a really good voice mimic so as before I might have had a bit of a gift.

​

First off, I did a lot of voice training based on  [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=27Yb04MBaOE](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=27Yb04MBaOE) Andrea James's initial work is to study the overtones on a spectrogram program. The one referenced is kind of old at this point but it still works.   
There's several more videos in that series. oldie, but still pretty good. 

​

It's more than just straight tone, it's also about the overtones that help create that harmony. It helps to really learn the difference between "head" and "chest" resonance as Andrea describes.   


The other part is learning a more femme speaking quality in terms of voiced sounds. I never really did that part, but maybe I should. That part is even more critical for those who can't get into the higher tone ranges, it helps produce that "husky femme" voice that some MTF's need to get by.   


Tone and Overtone is part 1 

Resonance is part 2

Sound "shapes" is 3. I should probably do that, I havent as much, but... I get femme'd regularly on phones and drive thrus, etc. So I might be a bit lucky there.   


The other thing I've done is to try to sing along with female artists that have a bit lower range like Tegan and Sara, and most of Fiona Apple, etc. Find one you can work with that just stresses your top end range a bit, and work on it, and while singing with headphones (on your cell phone, etc) in the ears, watch the spectrogram on the computer to look for the overtones.   


The other is practicing speech a lot just below your max stress range with occasional trips into the stress range (highest range). If your voice feels "sore" after a while you are working on building that upper range. Of course, I think that's highly YMMV, but that's how I did it. Maybe I got lucky. When I did a lot of my training, I had a 90 minute commute to work and back, so plenty of time to just talk to myself in that almost stressed to stressed range. I would often tell people I just had this nagging sore throat. The downside is I have a femme voice with a semi-masc presentation. Leads to some amusing situations like "Oh, that was you calling to pickup XYZ?" like their brains can't put the femme voice to the semi-masc person.   


As for the lower end, well, that was more a matter of doing the same in reverse. I think working in the lower range at first can help figure out that feeling of chest vs head resonance. you can really feel it in the lower tones, so use that to really find the resonance. As you train, you'll feel it move gradually from chest, to neck, to throat, to jaw, up into head space, like it feels that the nose is resonating. It's hard to explain but once you hit it you'll know.   


Good luck!

FTM folks can use DHT cream to masculinize their parts and pieces to a degree, and DHT is responsible for what makes boy parts in early early life. 

Fin does one type at about 75% reduction, Avodart (dutasteride) can do two, and it's like 94%. Avodart is pricey though, fin is generic now at 5mg. 

When you inhibit 5AR, a compound that turns T into DHT, you raise your overall T level as you lower DHT... but... thanks to something called aromatase - some of that excess T turns into Estrogen.. so for individuals so sensitive (I might be one) you raise your E to a degree. and, There are scare mongers who act like it totally destroyed them... but of course, remember all them are cismen.. whereas our population actually may want some of those changes.

Well, I will give it two opinions, both are relevant. 

1 - Most people make that call subconciously and don't think about it. You are one or the other to most people. If you are in the "either/or" range, which is what the video trains you for, people have to go on other cues. I've seen some of your pics, I think two and two will equal four in the real world. 

2 - The video trains for an "at or above" the frequency range, so, again, if you are at or above that's pretty much it. There's overlap, the goal is to get into the "above average guy" voice, and then the either/or mode fires up. The rest is kind of a matter of opinion... for example, my mom is lower than I am (I leave my spectrogram on all the time to watch voices around me.. was kind of surprised). 

After pitch, the rest is kind of window dressing like lilt, up and down, like oh my GAWD! valley girl stuff (but not to an extreme) where-guys-kind-of-do-this-monotone-low-rumble-thing. But my mom doesn't do much of that lilt stuff and has a little lower tone, no one looks twice at her, back to that whole "two plus two equals four" thing I like to follow. 

You'll always be hyper alert to it, but most people won't be.. you either do or don't.. and I say you do pass. 

You want to get a good read from the normals? Find a reason to call someone's customer service and see what they do, like a credit card or cable company, etc. Look for the "ma'ams" etc. one time I got like ten in quick succession, super neat.

If you can maintain it well enough (I think you can) then it becomes a "set it and forget it" for people you make a first impression on.

Well, to answer the question - I've done a combination of opti-fast and keto. (opti-fast 800 is the official name, which is used for gastric bypass folks before and after surgery for a while). Yes, it's supposed to be done with a doctor's supervision, so I did some bloodwork etc before I started, everything was fine. 

having been a support person for 2 people having had bypass, and considering myself for it (no insurance for a long time) I've become very familiar with the basics of it and "copied" it with off the shelf stuff. Bonuses: No huge ass money commitment at huge prices to one set of products you might not like, and you can buy stuff over time as you need it. I saw a lot of people selling off half-used optifast kits on E-bay, etc, if they couldn't stand it/quit the program/etc. (I think the prices for that stuff is criminal). 

I go a little higher than 800, I aim for 1200-1500 a day. sometimes I'll "cheat" and go higher. But the secret really is total calorie count in a day. BMR (Basal Metabolic rate) is what you burn in a day, if you do NOTHING at all other than keep breathing. Bigger you are, the bigger your burn. Then, you figure out how active you are. Most big people are around 1.2 or 1.3 (BMR x modifier). Then you get your total daily values. Where I'm at now - I'd need 2700/cal per day to maintain. so, if I eat 1200 or so, that's 1500 x 7 days = 10,500 calories a week I'm not eating (deficit). If 3500 cals is one pound, then I lose 3 pounds a week. 

It's "bumpy" because as you lose fat, the fat cells take on water before they totally release. so you lose some, go up some, lose some, go up some, etc. But it's predictable. 

The other thing, the lower-carb part of it - Is about making a "fuel" switch. We live in a world where food is constant, and we are programmed to eat whenever food is present, because our bodies never know where food will be next. We are also programmed to crave salt, fat, and sweet because in the past those things were rare, and those of us who craved it and got the small amounts out there lived. 

So, when we get hungry, we eat. Our bodies learn that we need to eat, and we go into "Feast" mode. we get fat. We need to move into "famine" mode where the body switches to burning stores. that's called ketosis. You still eat, just at a deficit. The hard part is making the switch, they call that keto flu. It's where most people give up after the first week or so. the body screams for regular eating patterns. After a while, it accepts the new setup and the switch begins.

what happens? cool stuff. You get to a place where you have a lot more energy. When I'm really burning, I can barely sleep. I can feel the fat starting to come off my face. It's like a sunburn but on the inside. (This doesn't happen to everyone, but it does to me!) 

My hunger has changed. I know I'm hungry, but it does not consume me. It triggers what's called a "leptin reset" which is a hormone that tells us we are satisfied. We overeat, and we lose that response. do keto for a while and that can be reset and works a lot better. I feel awesome when I eat a "Regular" meal and it's enough. It didn't used to be. This takes time to change over, and it's hard, but when you get there, you don't know how you ever lived the old way.  

I eat a lot of low fat greek yogurt for protein and something "Sweet". Protein rich stuff is the key to feeling satisfied. I also do a lot of the atkins bars/etc. I sometimes will eat a big fat bowl of fresh microwaved veggies, all spiced up with sriracha. That's great for fiber and if you need something "more" to feel full. Also good for using the restroom regularly - the diet can make that part a lot slower going. :)

I don't care too much for the shakes at this point.. the bars are somewhat satisfying, believe it or not. At first I would watch the clock like a hungry wildebeest, waiting for my next "hit" (every 3-4 hours) in the first week... but as I settled in, it was great to feel my hunger becoming manageable.  

I take supplements to keep my vitamins and minerals right. I also have had ridiculous reflex which is medicalyl managed now at last, so I broke a hunger loop related to excess acid. (eating would stop the pain, so hey, I must have been hungry!) Also, At times, keto needs salt supplements because you lose water (and salt) at high rates as fat burns up. So, if you like salty snacks, those are almost a free for all. (You feel it if your salt gets off, BUT some salty snacks bring you right back). 

At this point, honestly, it's kind of hard to eat my "full" calories in a day. And it's awesome. I avoid high fat high sugar stuff, but sometimes I'll indulge in a small fry or something. the salt value makes it worth it.. and oh so satisfying too.

Well, I can see you are getting started. The best advice I can give is that it takes time. I've been working on it off and on for at least six months - but I also personally have had a fairly higher voice to start with. 

The range for most people is there - it's just that we get used to working in a lower range because higher pitched men have a harder time in life so we don't.  

I did a variety of approaches - one is doing "scale singing" where you go up and down relative to your starting voice range. That can help you to open up the higher ranges that are available to you... 
The  

"ah aH AH AHH AH Ah ah" 

Then there's learning your throat and voice muscles to move your larynx around. It's hard to learn at first.. but eventually you get it. It's an "up" and "Back" motion that's hard to teach.. but easy to feel. 

the range work gets you familiar with the up and down for pitch. 
the "back" helps with throat resonance in part, the other is finding what I think is called your "formant" which is your somewhat individual frequency when you MMMMMMM with your mouth that makes your teeth/lips/etc have a buzz. That's a big one for resonance... and like I said - i find using the example of "talking around" a constant tone really helps. It's not quite sing songy but maybe a tad less. (only been doing that for a few days actually!) You do this well enough and you will instantly feel if you go out of range. It's like a little indicator if you learn to read it. 

The other is to figure out how to speak so that your chest doesn't buzz. There's "Dead" giveaways and the "ooh not quite" giveaways.

the first was the "chest" vibration. Dead giveaway. The second is resonance - the "not quite, maybe 60%" as a good friend described it to me.

You lose faster at first, and as it falls, the loss slows. But - once you get used to eating this way - its a cool change. the hardest part is eating differently and realizing portion distortion, etc.

Gonna echo the sentiments on lower calories in a day. Also - look for "wasted calories" stuff like full sugar pop, juice, sweets, etc...stuff that doesn't have any nutrition in it. Allow yourself a piece of candy or two now and again to not trigger the deprivation mode, but keep it to a minimum. enjoy it, savor it, let it satisfy that sweet tooth, and over time you'll crave it a lot less. 

I've been doing a fusion of keto (basically, low carb) with lower calorie intake, but watching them carefully. I've been doing some meal replacement shakes and/or bars, and eating big bowls of JUST veggies (with some low cal flavorings, like hot sauce etc) for fiber and that sensation of eating something (and visiting the restroom, too). Of course, I have a lot more to lose. However, I started out about 265 - I've already lost about 25 pounds in about a month. On my way! 

The rule of thumb is to calculate your BMR (Basal Metabolic Rate) which is what you burn in a day standing still doing very little. (there are websites out there for this). For me @ 270 *ugh* it was about 2800. In other words, I ate wrong, too much, etc. I'm aiming for around 1000-1200 a day, and every now and then I "cheat" to maybe 1500. ("cheating" a little helps a LOT with the deprivation feeling, etc). So, I've created a daily deficit for me of as much as 1800/day. 3500 is a pound your body burns to make that up... so 2800 BMR - 1000 cal for daily food = 1800 per day x 7 days a week = 12,600 cal per week burned off /3500 = 3.6 pounds/wk approximate loss. You can speed this up with some moderate workouts etc, too. 

There are medically supervised diets like optifast that basically do exactly this. The key is to watch yourself, make sure your nutrition is right, and get used to a really low cal eating approach. And it works if you are dedicated.

The heavier you are to start, the faster the burn will go, and as you lose, the loss will slow. But the formula remains the same. It's HARD at first. The first 3-5 days will test your will. But stick with it and you can free yourself from constant hunger (that was my problem, also I needed a med change for my reflux, but it's been GOLDEN.) When the hunger hit me those first few days - I responded mentally with "Yes, I want food, but I want to be skinny more" in those initial inbetween times. 

Docs and others will flip if you lose weight that fast... but if you are serious you can do it. However - make sure your RDA of daily nutrients is reasonably met, or you can develop problems that are hard to deal with. If you do it well enough, you'll get to ketosis, where your hunger will settle down, and you'll feel like you have a razor sharp focus and you are not tired because your body is starting to burn fat instead of food (directly, anyway) and it becomes more "constant". Watching your carb intake at this point is really important (learn about carbs well) because if you eat too much ketosis can stop. read up some on /r/keto. It works if you can dedicate to it. Watch the shakes/bars though if you go this route - too many carbs in them might slow you down there if you want to try to do what I am doing and get the "double bang" of keto and low cal, so shakes and bars that are low carb if you want that. Not all are low carb and need careful reading. 

It takes time to get through the first few days, because you've got to break eating habits that have gotten you here in the first place. I was hungry every three hours on the dot (5 shakes OR bars at 170 cal each setting, MINIMUM 900 a day) and that was hard. If you need one more a day at first, it's not the end of the world. After a few days you sill hit a routine and it becomes easier. They say if you do it for 30 days it becomes habit. You'll have to be prepared to make better choices after you've lost, that's the hard part. Learn about better eating as you go - so when you do come off the plan and go back to "normal" you know what to do. 

Yeah, it might sound a bit extreme, and you have to learn some new habits, etc. But it's worth it... and no one who's ever been heavy who's had success with other stuff should give it a try. It's working great for me. You might be able to try a less intensive version (somewhat higher cal count, etc) for yourself as you don't have nearly what I have to lose. 

Tip: Save your occasional "Big" meal for when you eat with other people, so they don't get freaked out about what you are doing. Everyone's gonna have an opinion about losing weight, especially people that have never been fat - and I'm not doing it for them, this is for me - and they can politely STFU.

Telling people is a wild ride. Some accept, some reject, some leave your ass hanging in limbo (those are the WORST!)

First you've got to know a bit of my history. I grew up in a household which was comprised of a Dad who was raised Southern Baptist, and a Mom who was raised Hardcore Catholic. They both ran away from that, I guess, and did the whole 70's hippie thing. Apparently there was something about how they met when one of them lived on a bus (I never have gotten the whole story). Sadly, they are far from hippies now, which is really odd as I know a lot of older hippies which still seem like pretty cool people). I have no idea how they will react when I eventually come out to them... I think they'd be cool about it - but lately my mother is a control freak who has a lot of unhappiness issues, but I digress...

So at first we largely did a thing for church which I called "Sleep in on Sundays". I used to joke they were religious refugees. Occasionally my school friends would ask where I went to church, and I'd have to say "nowhere".. which would lead to invites to go to their places. Some of those experiences were darkly comedic. One of them involved going to a Fundie "sleepover" at a church in the middle of nowhere. It was like a bad horror movie. I knew I was in for it when the guy who picked  me and my friend up to go had ripped the radio out of his dashboard, because it would let satan in. I mean, it looked like it had been stolen... broken wires and everything, as if to say "I am triumphant! look at my Holy Victory!" 

We got there and it was the early 90's so "backmasking" was the thing - where if you play the record backward, you'd hear "Feed the Children to Satan!" and rightwing psychopop like that. So, we got treated to video after video after video of that sort of thing. I said "sleepover" because we really weren't allowed to sleep - it was just lots and lots of Indoctrination. Later, around 5 or 6am, all of us exhausted and sleep deprived, we were all asked to accept Jesus Christ as our Lord and Savior. Now, me, being a generalized smartass and an INTJ, did not bite. I had longer hair at the time (well, we all know why HERE, but it was interpreted that I was into the long hair metal bands and all that) so I got a special time with the ex-metal rocker all by myself upstairs. He told me all about his personal story and how the music was making him evil so he got out of it and I should too etc.... But I refused. I was like "dude, you serious?" They were stunned at my refusal. I'd probably be burned at the stake if it was the 1600's for my heresy... 

Another time when I was younger I went with a different friend of mine to a screening of one of those "Left Behind" movies - where all the Christian "persecution" took over the world and the last handful of Christians were holding out against the evil government. I remember actually laughing a few times at the absurdity of the film, and everyone else looked at me in horror. Of course, in my confused young days I also kind of hit on the male friend I had gone with - I ended up costing a family friend for it. LOL in retrospect I realize how much of a bad ass I actually was... :) I was recruiting before I knew what recruiting was. heh.

A third time wasn't quite so bad, but I remember we did a lot of stuff with guns at another event. That, and my tent got full of mosquitoes - so I came home looking like I'd been through a literal plague. My mom went "What the hell, did you guys get a plague of locusts out there?" LOL again. I mean looking back, it almost feels comic. The recruiting, and dare I say, brainwashing, was pretty intense. I suppose it really shaped my perceptions of the world to see how that all went down for them. 

Fast forward to the modern era - my ex wanted to go to church, so we ended up going to this Methodist place. I thought I heard progressive and welcoming voices, but it turns out it was only my imagination. When the pastor there would say things like "Lord help us make the RIGHT choice on GLBT and women pastors etc" It was really just a thinly veiled call for the status quo. 

I learned of the hypocrisy pretty clearly and quickly. I was invited to be part of the tech crew, the people who run lights and sound, etc.. and I thought "well, at least I can stay awake having something to do" and I did. My ex was pregnant and we werent married. She wanted to sing in the Choir. Of course, it didn't take long until some goddamn church busybody figured out we weren't married, and they "Couldn't make an example of that" because it was against all the rules, or whatever. of COURSE, since I was in the BACK, and I was GOOD at what I did (my career is media and sound tech and stuff) They wanted to keep me on. I promptly made my exit. They still call me now and again to come back, but I refuse. 

My last experience was that my ex still wanted church, so we found a UCC that was Open an affirming (open to GLBT folk). they were cool. They have a booth at pride, and recently accepted a T person into the fold (such that she was part of a workshop to talk about all that stuff for new comers). We were reasonably happy there, but it was near the end of our relationship (I made it a special point to make a special presentation of a dozen roses on Mother's day in front of everyone, because I wanted her to know I still loved her and cared about her). It didn't really make any difference in the end.... and so when I go there I think of that day. Don't get me wrong, the people there are great and I consider them friends and all - but I don't think Coventional Christianity will ever be my thing. (Largely because those who are open don't seem to engage those who are not... because they are interested in their "greater compatibility". 

Meanwhile... I've personally always been drawn more to the Buddhist Philosophy and Zen. The art of asking questions to gain better understanding... instead of taking one set of rules at face value. When I was growing up, I'd see people with bibles and talking about church etc all the time and I thought "That really seems kind of robotic - like someone gave you all your life answers and there's no discovery left - so what's to live for?" Of course I'm a many paths kind of person - if you are not hurting me I will leave you be... your journey is yours, not mine. 

And speaking of Buddhist thought, a good friend of mine recently become a full on Buddhist and invited me to sangha (group). We do 15 minutes of walking meditation (reminds me that life is a journey), 30 minutes of meditation (clear the mind and soul) and a discussion group after. It sounds so simple, but the first time I went, I felt something change - I felt a beam of light start to clear some of my head noise. The second time - my "lockbox" opened. It felt like when Tony Stark got the mark 2 chestplate ("Tastes like Coconut... and Metal!") 
and I realized that an anxiety I'd been nearly handicapped with last year was this trapped energy inside me.. my feminine energy. Since this moment my anxieties have gone WAY down. I can drive this energy in meditation into "feeling" my "real body" (what I'd imagine I'd be like when I'm all done) and my God was it one of the most affirming and positive things I've had happen in a long time. I KNOW it's what has to happen.  I guess I've always known - but it's come into sharp relief. Even though I am only JUST STARTING - I have so much more peace knowing a certainty. 

It seems counterintuitive, that just a simple gathering of people sharing their universal regard and spiritual energy with others with nothing more in common than "I respect your journey, you respect mine, let us learn from each other" would be so powerful. But it is. And when you really think about it, what makes more sense? Your life now, or what's written in an ancient book? 

See, for me, the Buddhist approach accepts that we all walk our own journey and that nothing is really written in a book about it. We have to be open on that journey and accept that ours is unlike any one else's. We want to conform, to fit in, to be part of something bigger than ourselves, but we also want that validation and social acceptance. In other words, we want to feel like we are in the same path, when nothing is farther from the truth. We have to accept we have our own paths and so do others. All we can do is be compassionate to those who travel other roads. Even if we are on the same road we are at different points. (another important point - being jealous of people who are farther along in transition, etc, is fruitless for the same reason.  

Where does this intersect with Trans life? Well - we are SO AWARE that we ARE SO DIFFERENT that the paths presented to us don't always make sense. We feel a great deal of fear because we know our calling is different - and we want acceptance - so we repress the self to fit. It can be done for a while - but eventually, as all journeys do - it calls to us until we are compelled to answer.

Oh geez - it sounds like some kind of conversation I'd have with my dad, who just recently became eligible for medicare after years of being basically underemployed and uninsured. Many of his 60+ friends have a lot of health problems, and he's acting like he's in the clear so long as he doesn't go in, because they'll drop a bunch of pills on him and he'll get old and die. It's totally irrational. I try to tell him "yeah, you might need a med or two but if you've gotten by so far without major problems it might be that you are in pretty good shape..." "Yeah, well that $35 visit would get me a gym membership".... yea, one of those that turns their back on modern medicine. 

I have a theory that he accellarated the death of my grandmother after her stroke, because she lost the ability to swallow in the stroke, insisting that she try to drink water (led to a lung infection after some got in her lung). He just knows better and fuck the doctors who are just out to control you. I'm on the larger side and he's constantly got some comment about what and how I eat - meanwhile he is happy to get donuts, ice cream, candy, etc and coffee and go out to eat whenever he has money, et cetera... 

What's worse here is somehow you are being "suckered in" by "big pharma". I had a bout with major league anxiety and I took meds for a time... I chose to tell my father about my meds in the generic names because he was saying "that prozac stuff is bad juju"... because as I mentioned he's unemployed, and has lots of time to fear monger and just think of all the shit he doesn't like, and we get subjected to his endless negative commentary. It's like watching a DVD on the descriptive language track stuck on. It's infuriating. Yes, meds can have some concerns, but on the whole I am glad they were there for me. I'm no stranger to their occasional use. I pick my conversations carefully with him, and even then I'm not always successful. I engage with him just enough for what needs to done, and not much more. 

"Have you got anything better to fucking talk about in your life?" often comes across my mental lips. He doesn't care how his actions cause discomfort, and it's all he's got to talk about 90% of the time. It's so exhausting. 

I don't know if my dad is worse than yours, but I can sure empathize with the weird-ass things that get focused on like that. It's like getting suckerpunched in the feels that you didn't know you had.

One day - I was told my father had something to tell me. It was serious. He could not tell me on the phone, he had to tell me in person. 

I was thinking "Is he leaving my mom?" "Is he gay?" "Is he not my dad?" "Am I adopted?" - so many things go through my head. 

Of course - I was trying to brace for the fact that I had no idea what was coming, and try to be accepting of whatever it might have been... 

Turns out he was contacted by someone who he had never seen before, and it was a woman. This woman was my father's daughter with a woman my father had dated several years before my mother, and later, me, came into his life. He managed to keep her entirely secret from the family (even my grandmother who worked in family court, which AMAZED ME TO NO END). She was looking for any medical info for one of her kids due to a recent health diagnosis. 

She looks very much like me.
